results.title: carbon emissions / road traffic essay
results.known: 22 out of 25. Marker not yet specified — confirm whether this was a teacher or an examiner before treating it as a firm anchor (same standard applied to Test 2).

issues.text: The statement 'MPC=MSC' after taxation is inaccurate; the correct condition is 'MPC+tax = MSC'.
The claim that a maximum price set below equilibrium may be set 'too high or low' is contradictory, as a price below equilibrium cannot be too high.

results.improvement: Replace the sentence 'MPC=MSC' with 'MPC+tax = MSC' to correctly describe the effect of the tax on marginal private cost.

results.title: National Minimum Wage / social care essay
results.known: 19–20 out of 25, marked by the teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-13). Originally reported only as "mid A", which is a grade band rather than a mark — the real figure was obtained rather than inferred from a grade boundary, since guessing it and then treating the guess as ground truth is exactly the substitution this project exists to prevent. Kept as a range, which is honest, rather than forced to one number.

issues.text: The essay states "MPC is less than MSC" for a positive externality, which reverses the correct relationship (MSC < MPC).
The link between higher wages and lower unit labour cost is asserted without explaining the mechanism (e.g., how productivity offsets wage rises).

results.improvement: Correct the statement to "MSC is less than MPC" and briefly explain that a positive externality means the social marginal cost is lower than the private marginal cost, which helps clarify why higher wages can lead to under‑production and affect firm profitability.
